title: U-19 Cricketer Nandini, 17, Dies by Suicide in Telangana; Family Alleges Harassment
excerpt: The Vikarabad teenager had recently been selected for a BCCI Under-19 team, according to reports. Her family has accused two men of harassing her, and police have registered a case of suspicious death.
body:
• Nandini, 17, a cricketer from Sangayya Palli village in Telangana's Vikarabad district, died by suicide on Friday, November 13. She had recently been selected for a BCCI Under-19 team, according to media reports.
  • Her family alleges that two men, identified as Anil and Krishna, had been following and harassing her. The allegations have not been established, and police say the investigation is ongoing.
  • Police have registered a case of suspicious death based on her father's complaint, seized her mobile phone for forensic examination, and were searching for the two men, according to reports.
  • If you or someone you know is struggling, help is available in India around the clock: Tele-MANAS on 14416 and the KIRAN helpline on 1800-599-0019.

Nandini, a 17-year-old cricketer from Vikarabad district in Telangana, died by suicide on Friday, November 13, according to reports from the district. She had recently been selected for a BCCI Under-19 team, according to media reports, a milestone that had marked her out as one of the district's most promising young players.

Nandini was a native of Sangayya Palli village in Yalal mandal. She was staying at her grandmother's house in Madhu Colony in Vikarabad town, where she was continuing her studies alongside cricket coaching. She was alone at home when she died, according to reports.

What the family alleges

After her death, Nandini's parents and relatives alleged that harassment led to it. The family claims that a young man named Anil had been following and harassing her in the name of love for the past few days, and that another young man, identified as Krishna, had assisted him. The family alleged that Nandini was distressed by the harassment and demanded strict action against those responsible.

These are allegations made by the family. They have not been established, and police say the circumstances of the death are still being investigated.

Family members and local residents staged a road protest in Vikarabad demanding the immediate arrest of the two men, according to reports.

What police say

Police received information about the death at around 9 a.m. on Friday and reached the spot, Vikarabad Circle Inspector Raghu said, according to reports of his remarks. He said the initial investigation indicated that Nandini had died by suicide.

Based on a complaint filed by Nandini's father, police registered a case of suspicious death and launched an investigation, according to Hyderabad Mail. Her body was shifted to a hospital for a postmortem examination. Police seized Nandini's mobile phone and sent it for forensic examination as part of the investigation, and officers were reportedly searching for the two men named by the family.

Circle Inspector Raghu also appealed to parents to maintain open communication with their children and to pay attention to their emotional and personal difficulties, according to reports.

What happens next

The forensic examination of the phone and the postmortem process are the next steps investigators have described publicly. Police have not announced any arrests, and further details of the investigation are awaited.
